evidence.field: Summary; source; permission; license; other versions
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 能-seal.svg as a drawing of 能 in Shuowen seal-script style. It points to Hanziyuan image S07257 and Sinica image record 27.80FD as sources. The page also records Richard Sears permission and says the Sinica picture is CC0 1.0; the Commons file is marked CC0. This supports selecting it as an illustrative Shuowen-style seal form, not as an independently dated artifact or evidence for the disputed Shang identification. The page lists separate Shang, bronze, slip, and other script versions, so this seal drawing should not stand in for those forms.

evidence.text: The Commons file page attributes its seal image to the Sinica database and says that image is CC0 1.0, while also noting Richard Sears permission/copyright material. Commons’ agreement page says publication under its stated terms was approved by the copyright holder and archived in a VRT ticket. The selected file is a derivative digital drawing; these records provide provenance and reuse context, not the historical age of the glyph.

evidence.text: The provided candidate named Shuowen Seal Radical 380.svg could not be opened directly. The inspected Commons seal-script category explains that radical numbers index seal ideographs and lists Radical 380 as one ideograph in a Unicode seal-script block; that label alone does not verify that the file depicts 能. The Commons category for 能 lists the filename, but this is insufficient to establish its identity or source image. Do not select this candidate without the exact file page and image being inspectable.

evidence.text: The page presents a sequence of forms labeled Shang, Western Zhou, Spring and Autumn, Warring States, Chu slips, Qin slips, and Shuowen seal, and classifies 能 as a pictograph for a bear. This is an accessible secondary presentation of the graph tradition, but the table does not by itself settle the disputed identification of damaged Shang forms or establish a dated earliest occurrence.

Both direct original-image opens failed. The exact Radical 380 page could not be accessed; Commons search/category evidence listed the filename but did not verify its image identity. Opened the Chinese Wiktionary character page for its ancient-forms table.

Search returned the 能 category listing the candidate filename and the seal ideograph category explaining radical indexing. Inspected the radical-category description and Commons’ Richard Sears permission agreement. Direct file page remained inaccessible.

gaps: The Commons page supports identifying 能-seal.svg as a Shuowen-style seal drawing and gives linked Sinica/Hanziyuan image records, but the browser could not open the direct SVG original or Sinica character page. The drawing was therefore not independently visually inspected in this research session.

Shuowen seal style is a later script category and does not independently establish the form or use of the disputed Shang inscriptions, nor does it resolve the bear-versus-ability semantic relationship.

The exact Shuowen Seal Radical 380.svg page and image were inaccessible. Its character identity, provenance, and file-specific licensing remain unverified; do not curate it based on the filename or category listing alone.

The source page has mixed provenance notes: it attributes the picture to Sinica CC0 while also noting Richard Sears permission/copyright material. It is reasonable to cite the file page and its stated CC0 status, but do not treat the page as a bulk-reuse grant for all material in the upstream databases.
